headline: A cold, dry start gives way to a high-impact Wednesday rain and wind system; Kentucky turns wet Wednesday afternoon while a strengthening cold-air-damming storm brings heavy rain and gusty northeast wind to the Upstate
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: Low clouds break as colder and drier air settles across the Bluegrass today. Clear conditions and light north wind allow a hard freeze tonight, followed by a sunny but chilly Tuesday. Clouds increase Tuesday night as southern- and northern-stream disturbances begin interacting. Rain spreads into Central Kentucky Wednesday afternoon, becoming widespread Wednesday night and continuing through the early-Thanksgiving 72-hour endpoint; gusty wind and reduced visibility become the main travel concerns.
kentucky.currentConditions: At 8:15 AM EST, KDVK reported 43°F with a 41°F dew point, northwest wind near 9 mph, 10-mile visibility, scattered clouds near 600 feet and an overcast near 1,100 feet. At 8:55 AM, KLEX reported 43°F with north wind near 12 mph, gusting near 18 mph, and a broken ceiling near 2,200 feet. No official NWS point alert was active for Danville at the final issuance check.

days.label: Monday / Monday night
days.precipitation: 10% or less; dry after the early morning
days.hazard: OFFICIAL NWS ALERT STATUS: no active point alert covers Danville at issuance. The independent concern is a hard freeze tonight, especially in sheltered rural valleys. Daytime north wind will add a chill, but flooding, thunder and hazardous wind are not expected.
days.forecast: Morning low clouds continue breaking, followed by partly to mostly sunny, chilly weather. North wind runs 7–12 mph with gusts around 18–25 mph. The most-likely Danville high is near 53°F. Clear sky, diminishing wind and dry air then support a rapid evening temperature drop, with a most-likely Tuesday-morning low near 26°F after applying the maintained Danville cold correction; colder valleys may reach the lower 20s.

days.label: Tuesday / Tuesday night
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert covers Tuesday at issuance. Independent concerns are another freeze Tuesday night and a chilly northeast breeze. Rain, thunder and hazardous wind are not expected during this day.
days.forecast: Mostly sunny, dry and chilly beneath strong high pressure, with a most-likely high near 47°F. Northeast wind runs 5–10 mph with occasional gusts of 15–25 mph. Clouds increase late Tuesday night as the next system organizes, but the night remains dry. The most-likely early-Wednesday low is near 31°F.

days.label: Wednesday / early Thanksgiving
days.precipitation: 20–30% through early afternoon; 70–80% by evening; 90% overnight and early Thanksgiving
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert covers Wednesday at issuance. Independent concerns are widespread rain, wet holiday-travel roads, reduced visibility and increasingly gusty wind Wednesday night into early Thanksgiving. Thunder and flooding are not the primary signals. A late-Thanksgiving wet-snow possibility is beyond this 72-hour endpoint.
days.forecast: Clouds thicken during the morning, with rain most likely reaching Danville between about 3–9 PM EST; a 1–11 PM onset remains plausible. Rain becomes widespread Wednesday evening and overnight as the upper disturbances begin phasing and a coastal low strengthens. The most-likely high is near 53°F and the most-likely overnight low is near 40°F. East wind around 5–12 mph becomes more variable and gusty overnight, with gusts of 20–30 mph possible by early Thanksgiving. About 0.25–0.60 inch of rain is expected through Wednesday night, with additional rain early Thursday and after the 10 AM endpoint.

kentucky.bottomLine: Central Kentucky turns sunnier but remains chilly today, followed by a hard freeze tonight. Most-likely Danville high/low pairs are 53/26°F, 47/31°F and 53/40°F. Tuesday stays dry. Rain develops mainly Wednesday evening, becomes widespread Wednesday night and remains in progress at the early-Thanksgiving endpoint, with wet roads and increasing wind affecting holiday travel.
kentucky.confidence: High in today's clearing and hard freeze; high in Tuesday's dry, chilly weather; medium-high in Wednesday rain and medium in its exact onset, temperature and early-Thanksgiving wind

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson primary · Central/Pickens County comparison
upstate.summary: Low stratus and patchy fog lift slowly today before a warm afternoon. A dry frontal passage tonight brings a cooler, breezy Tuesday and rebuilds a classic cold-air-damming wedge. Rain and northeast wind increase rapidly Wednesday as a strengthening coastal storm approaches; heavy rain, 30–40 mph gusts and localized power or drainage problems are possible Wednesday afternoon through early Thanksgiving. The storm will still be underway at the 72-hour endpoint.
upstate.currentConditions: Around 9:35–9:45 AM EST, Clemson, Central and nearby Upstate observations continued to show mist or fog and IFR to LIFR ceilings, including ceilings near 200–300 feet in parts of the corridor. Surface wind remained light. The earlier official Special Weather Statement for locally dense fog expired at 9 AM, and no official NWS point alert was active for Clemson or Central at the final check. Tempest data was not used.

days.label: Monday / Monday night
days.hazard: OFFICIAL NWS ALERT STATUS: no active point alert covers Clemson or Central at issuance; the earlier fog statement expired at 9 AM. The independent concern is lingering very low ceilings and localized fog through late morning. Flooding, thunder and hazardous wind are not expected today.
days.forecast: Mist and very low clouds lift gradually toward late morning or noon, followed by partial sunshine and a warm afternoon. West to west-northwest wind remains around 0–5 mph. The most-likely corridor high is near 71°F. Mostly cloudy conditions return tonight as a weak dry front passes and northeast flow begins, with a most-likely regional low near 49°F.

days.label: Tuesday / Tuesday night
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert covers Tuesday at issuance. The independent concern is a breezy northeast wind. Widespread advisory-level wind, freezing temperatures, fog and rain are not expected.
days.forecast: Partly sunny, dry and cooler as strong high pressure builds north of the area. The most-likely corridor high is near 58°F. East-northeast wind runs 7–14 mph, becoming northeast 8–16 mph Tuesday night, with gusts of 22–30 mph. Clouds increase overnight as the wedge strengthens, with a most-likely regional low near 39°F.

days.label: Wednesday / early Thanksgiving
days.precipitation: 70–85% after 9 AM; 90–100% Wednesday afternoon, Wednesday night and early Thanksgiving
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert covers Wednesday at issuance. Independent concerns are heavy rain, localized poor-drainage flooding or ponding, difficult holiday travel, strong northeast gusts and isolated power outages. Thunder and wintry precipitation are not expected.
days.forecast: A classic cold-air-damming wedge remains entrenched as low pressure strengthens near the Southeast coast. Rain begins around 8–10 AM and becomes widespread, with periods of heavy rain Wednesday afternoon and night. The most-likely high is near 51°F and the most-likely overnight low is near 44°F. Northeast wind increases to 14–22 mph with gusts commonly 30–40 mph; isolated gusts of 45–50 mph cannot be ruled out. Rainfall through the 10 AM Thursday endpoint should total 1.00–2.25 inches, with localized totals near or above 3 inches where a focused band persists. Rain and gusty wind remain in progress Thursday morning.

upstate.bottomLine: Very low clouds and localized fog lift slowly today, followed by a warm afternoon. Most-likely corridor high/low pairs are 71/49°F, 58/39°F and 51/44°F. Tuesday is cooler, breezy and dry. Rain and northeast wind increase quickly Wednesday, with heavy rain, gusts of 30–40 mph and localized flooding or power concerns continuing into early Thanksgiving. Tempest remains excluded.
upstate.confidence: Moderate in today's cloud-clearing rate and high temperature; high in Tuesday's cooler dry wedge; high in Wednesday rain, but medium in exact temperature, rainfall maximum and strongest gust placement

sourceNotes: Chris Bailey's November 23 Kentucky Weather Center post and supporting graphics were accepted as authoritative source material for Kentucky. Bailey supports widespread Thanksgiving rain, 30–40 mph gust potential, falling temperatures and a conditional later wet-snow chance; only the portion through the early-Thanksgiving endpoint is included here.

Official NWS alerts are kept separate from the independent forecast. No active point alert covered Danville, Clemson or Central at the final check; the earlier Upstate dense-fog statement expired before issuance.
Fresh NWS Greenville-Spartanburg guidance favors the slower EPS/AIFS-style storm cluster over the faster GEFS-style cluster, supporting a higher-impact Upstate rain and wind forecast.
The Upstate Wednesday temperature remains model-sensitive: fresh GFS/RRFS profiles are colder than official guidance. The 47–54°F range and most-likely 51°F explicitly resolve that bounded conflict.
The Central Kentucky Wednesday high depends on rain onset. The forecast uses 53°F within a 50–56°F range and places widespread rain mainly after afternoon onset.

Fresh Danville GFS, GEFS and ECMWF GRIB files were downloaded and extracted. Clean temperature, wind and moisture fields were reviewed; the local GRIB precipitation totals were excluded because the validator flagged an ECMWF cumulative-precipitation bookkeeping inconsistency.
The successful 13:17Z College of DuPage audit was used. A 14:47Z automated recheck returned no model files, so no later COD cycle was substituted without evidence.
Legacy NAM, NAM 3-km Nest, SREF and HiResW files dated November 4 or earlier were stale and excluded.
COD radar showed both forecast regions precipitation-free at the latest analysis, while satellite imagery showed no deep local convection.
Tempest data was excluded from all Upstate analysis and verification.
Daily lows are following-night lows. The third cards extend only through the exact 72-hour endpoint on early Thanksgiving; conditions later Thanksgiving are outside this regular candidate.
